evidence:
The actual frozen WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx was opened with openpyxl: Quality Checks!A8:D8 identifies number 7, task_asks_for_a_real_working_product, and states "Real build work is required; a stub or trivial tweak can't earn the reward." Internal Quality Checks row 8 agrees. Frozen harbor-webdev-rubric-qc/references/quality-checks.md:33-35 asks for the smallest satisfying submission and rejects a static page, a single CRUD screen or a mock. This is a source-level product-demand judgment; the runtime rows remain separate under qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md.

The smallest conforming submission is a substantial browser code playground. Frozen task/instruction.md:1 requires authored JavaScript, HTML and CSS, preview and snippet library; line 3 requires last-good-preview recovery and two-editor overwrite protection; line 5 explicitly says there is no starter app. All six public notes were inspected. environment/instructions/behaviour.md:5-15 adds fresh JS/HTML contexts, CSS snapshot execution without old handlers, cancellation, a shared five-second source/callback deadline, interactive completed previews, rollback and exact source error lines. Its lines 19-29 require inspectable multi-level console history, debounce, exact save/load, title validation and revision-aware refusal with retained draft recovery. security.md:3-11 requires preview isolation, bounded unsupported-execution refusal and a separate snippet network boundary. integration.md:7 requires saved identities/revisions to survive a complete process restart. These are interacting stateful behaviors beyond CRUD. environment/Dockerfile:14-23 copies only notes/assets and initializes /app with .gitkeep; environment/assets/seed_data.json:3-4 supplies no snippets or implementation, so this cannot be completed by a trivial edit to shipped app code.

Reward prerequisites enforce basic working execution and shared storage. tests/gates/render/judge.toml:23-27 requires a newly chosen marker to result from pressing Run and to appear in both preview and console; it explicitly rejects a hardcoded sample or marker visible only in the editor. tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-29 requires a successful new UI write plus exact identity/title/filename/source retrieved via the library in a clean independent context, then again after reload; toast, health, static seed or localStorage alone is insufficient. tests/test.sh:213-225 runs gates and stops after a failed gate before scoring. tests/tools/score.py:40-48 makes reward zero if either gate is nonpositive and requires functional score >0.05. tests/scoring.toml supplies the canonical 0.6/0.2/0.2 weights. Functional criteria additionally cover execution/lifecycle, rollback, persistence and concurrency, rather than rewarding only the shell. The three scored prompts preserve the global prerequisite.

Adversarial source reasoning: a visually polished static editor with canned example output and a Save toast fails the authored-marker gate. A working single CRUD screen with a dead runner fails that same gate. An actual runner whose library merely writes localStorage and returns a successful no-op POST fails clean-context retrieval. These are evaluated against explicit observable requirements, not inferred package requirements. They were source counterexamples, not newly executed mutations. A conforming alternative using another frontend/editor, different labels, arbitrary observed API routes and server-rendered library responses is expressly allowed by policy.md:5, integration.md:3, the render gate's purpose-based controls and constraints gate:25-27. app_context.md:16 also prevents a missing Auto-run convenience control alone from defeating unrelated gate evidence. No credible static/mock false-pass or conforming-alternative false-fail was found for this row.

Supporting raw evidence: golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json facts.S02.js_html_filename_dispatch records authored JS body "js-dispatch-ok" with "js-dispatch-log", then HTML body "html-dispatch-ok\nTry handler" with "html-once-marker". facts.S22.process_restart_durability records identities 1-4 with exact fields/revisions before and after a successful canonical restart (PID 16 to 335). Its driver library_flow.cjs:37-40 compares the entire record list and loads both dedicated restart records before reporting the observation. facts.S23.stale_save_server_refusal records successful revisions 2 and 4 and rejected stale requests using revisions 1 and 3, with newer records unchanged in both editor directions; library_flow.cjs:59 and :72 explicitly fresh-read and compare the winner. Independently recomputed SHA256 for all 22 actual_app_files entries: every frozen golden file matches; functional judge and prompt hashes also match RESULTS.json. These scripted observations support the existence of real implementation work, but do not measure the full configured judge, actual weak-app rewards, Oracle or target-model score. No such score or overall QC clearance is claimed.
